questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk.

questions.question: When you pass a car that just parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, be ready for the driver to open the door. Drive carefully and stay alert near parked vehicles.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, if you are not the driver.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road. This applies to everyone in the car, not just the driver.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When entering a busy freeway, what should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Use the entrance ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots before you merge.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Share half a lane with the motorcycle.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and need a complete lane to drive safely. Even if there looks like room to share, motorcycles need space to move safely.

questions.question: When a car's bright headlights are blinding you, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from bright headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs tell you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you of railroad crossings. Yield to trains and do not try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: At night, if oncoming headlights are too bright, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road to reduce glare. Do not look at oncoming headlights. The bright light can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should only reduce your speed to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: The new speed limit begins right at this sign. You must slow down to 35 mph immediately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass is low. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: You see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road and stop. Let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over and stop.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give them room in front of your vehicle to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room in front of your vehicle to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down to create space in front of your car. This helps the other driver pass more easily and quickly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that railroad tracks are ahead. Watch for trains and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving puts you, your passengers, and others on the road in danger. Stay focused on driving to prevent crashes.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to enter the main road after a stop. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: Give the bus the right of way. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter the traffic.

questions.question: One of your tires blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep the steering wheel steady and slowly lift your foot off the gas pedal.
Maintain your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel steady and slowly lift your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal slowly. Once you have control, brake gently and pull over to a safe spot.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to create more distance between you and the tailgater.
Brake hard to force the other driver to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching drivers. If someone is following too closely, slow down to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two-way road means no driver can cross it to pass, no matter which direction they are traveling.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are extra slippery right after rain starts.
Allow extra space before you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires sit on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down during heavy rain or when there is standing water or slush to keep your wheels from sliding.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same full lane width as all other vehicles for safe operation.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop and then go when it is safe.
You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You may turn in the direction the arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow on a traffic light means you must stop completely and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.
